name: Central Amazon Old-Growth Lowland Forest
description: Central Amazon old-growth lowland rainforest on Oxisol: 11 agents, mycorrhizal fungi and pollinators keystone, 400 trees/ha on a 1,000 ha reference area; twelve edges into Canopy Trees and Understory are rescaled to the in-degree cap (Step 3.8). Small losses are priced linearly (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1). Agent value: de Groot et al. (2012) tropical forest without climate regulation, PPP-converted (Step 8e.5). Illustrative. Sources: gaia/cases/definitions/AMAZON_FOREST.md; derivations: CASE_NOTES.md there.

units_per_ha.note: Terra firme, DBH >= 10 cm: ~400-600 stems/ha, stated without a citation; sets the per-tree carbon.

unit_value.source: case author's choice ('Calibrated' in the docstring)
unit_value.note: Selective-logging revenue per tree (one-off); no market source.

safe_threshold_ratio.source: Lovejoy & Nobre (2018): Amazon tipping point at 20-25% deforestation (via AMAZON_FOREST.md §6)
safe_threshold_ratio.note: A basin-scale tipping point applied to a 1,000 ha patch, a scale mismatch (audit S4); under the area_loss damage model (Step 8d.1) the depletion beyond which the REMAINING resource starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs its average value.

agent[*].dependency_weight.note: Rated Medium in the case docstring; an expert judgement with no cited source.

edge[*].strength.note: Monte Carlo range (Step 8e.4, as Posidonia's): x0.5 to x1.5, a judgement for unfitted strengths, narrower than the placeholder x/÷3 that put almost every draw above the in-degree cap. Edges into an agent whose incoming strengths (keystone boosts included) exceed 1/1.5 of the cap rise at most to the cap: see their own range.

annual_value_per_ha.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2012.07.005, Table 2 (read in full): tropical forest, total economic value Int$5,264/ha/yr minus climate regulation Int$2,044 = Int$3,220/ha/yr (2007 international dollars, 2007 price level; 96 estimates, Table 3); converted to euros with the World Bank's PPP conversion factor for household final consumption (PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, the 'private consumption' series de Groot et al. used), Spain, 2007: 0.808165 EUR per international $ (World Development Indicators, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ESP/indicator/PA.NUS.PRVT.PP?date=2007&format=json, read 12 October 2026)
annual_value_per_ha.note: Every agent; the dependency weights split it (Step 8e.5, the owner's answer: re-based on de Groot et al. 2012). 3,220 x 0.808165 = EUR 2,602.29/ha/yr in 2007 euros at Spanish purchasing power: international dollars carry US purchasing power and must be converted with a country's PPP rate, not the market exchange rate (de Groot et al., footnote 5); Spain is the country of Gaia's euro figures (the Catalan Posidonia user); the euro area has no 2007 value in this series. At the 2007 market rate (0.7297 EUR/USD, PA.NUS.FCRF) it would be EUR 2,350. Not inflated to a later price year and no income adjustment (the owner's decision for benefit transfers, Step 8d.5). Climate regulation is left out because carbon is valued only by gaia.carbon (decision D3). Of the 3,220: provisioning 1,828 (food 200, water 27, raw materials 84, genetic 13, medicinal 1,504), regulating without climate 485, habitat 39, cultural (recreation) 867 (the rows sum to 3,219: rounding in Table 2). A global tropical-forest mean, not a Central Amazon valuation: the totals of the service medians (2,355 with climate) are less than half the means (Table 3), so low confidence and the default x/÷2 Monte Carlo range. It replaces EUR 580/ha/yr, the sum of the spec's partly unverified §8 anchors (audit S4). The EXPERIMENTAL pricing anchors (food 200, pollination 30, water 27) are parts of the 3,220, still used as EUR at face value.

steepness.note: Degradation of the REMAINING resource past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1, as for Posidonia): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span, the same curve for every agent. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. Not fitted to field data (calibration regime B). Monte Carlo range 6-18, uniform (Step 8e.4, as Posidonia: a judgement; the placeholder x/÷3 gave 4-36).

agents.name: Canopy Trees
agents.description: Emergent + canopy layer (400+ species/ha) — primary biomass, rainfall recycling

agents.name: Understory
agents.description: Sub-canopy trees, palms, ferns, epiphytes — shade-tolerant reproduction, microclimate regulation

agents.name: Mycorrhizal Fungi
agents.description: Arbuscular + ectomycorrhizae — KEYSTONE nutrient gateway on P-depleted Oxisol, non-substitutable

keystone_threshold.note: Health below which the agent's outgoing edges double; hand-set, no source. Monte Carlo range 0.10-0.40, uniform (Step 8e.4, Posidonia's +-0.15: a judgement; the placeholder x/÷3 reached 0.9-1.0, where the keystone boost would fire at almost any damage).

agents.description: Bees, butterflies, hummingbirds, bats — reproduction for 90%+ of canopy species

agents.description: Capybaras, sloths, leafcutter ants, insects — energy transfer, population dynamics

agents.name: Apex Predators
agents.description: Jaguars, harpy eagles — top-down population control, KEYSTONE trophic role

agents.name: Aquatic System
agents.description: River fish (3,000+ species), river dolphins, aquatic plants — nutrient transport, fisheries

agents.name: Epiphytes & Bromeliads
agents.description: Orchids, bromeliads, lichens (~25,000 species) — water retention, microhabitat creation

strength.note: Spec §3 value divided by 2.10 (into Canopy Trees) or 1.45 (into Understory) to the in-degree cap (Step 3.8, mechanical, ratios kept); not a fit. Monte Carlo range (Step 8e.4): x0.5 to x1.004. The incoming strengths into Canopy Trees sum to 0.996 of the in-degree cap of 1 (keystone boosts included), so the edges into it can rise only by x1.004 together before a draw breaks the cap; their documented values are therefore the top of their range (x1.004), not its middle. Drawn values are never rescaled.

stored_carbon_tonnes.source: 173 ± 12 Mg C/ha total biomass (AMAZON_FOREST.md §2, citing 'Phil Trans R Soc B, 227 plots', author not given) × 3.67 / 400 trees/ha
stored_carbon_tonnes.note: Matches the literature per the audit (S4); full citation pending (Step 8). Per tree at the 400 trees/ha reference density.

annual_absorption_tonnes.source: 0.62 t C/ha/yr old-growth net accumulation (AMAZON_FOREST.md §2, citing Wikipedia, 1975-1996 data) × 3.67 / 400
annual_absorption_tonnes.note: The literature review calls 0.62 a historic peak and recommends ~0.30-0.40 t C/ha/yr; not yet applied (audit S4).

soil_carbon_tonnes.note: ~40 t C/ha 'in roots' × 3.67 / 400, no cited source; the name is misleading (root, not soil carbon; audit S4).
